so help me God phrase

also as I live, I swear, honest to God, cross my heart, as heaven is my witness, so help me

classical

Plaut. Amph. 597: neque, ita mē dī ament, crēdēbam prīmō mihimet Sōsiae
Ter. And. 947: Ita mē dī ament, crēdō.

Ita mē dī ament

so help me God; as I hope for heaven’s love

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

“So may the gods love me”: an oath that what one says is true (Lewis & Short s.v. amō). Often followed by ut and the thing sworn to.

Other words

  • Ita mē dī amābunt — so help me God

    also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 496: Ita mē dī amābunt ut ego hunc auscultō lubēns.; Plaut. Poen. 1.3.30 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Examples

  • Ita mē dī amābunt ut ego hunc auscultō lubēns.

    So help me God, I do enjoy listening to this man.Plaut. Aul. 496

  • neque, ita mē dī ament, crēdēbam prīmō mihimet Sōsiae

    and, so help me God, at first I, Sosia, did not believe my own selfPlaut. Amph. 597

See also by Hercules!, honestly, I’ll be damned if …, bless you.

SourcesLewis & Short: amo

Plautus, Amphitruo 597; Aulularia 496. Terence, Andria 947.
